title: Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde

chapters.title: Dr. Jekyll Was Quite at Ease

stage.logMeta: Hyde’s dossier updated — seen face to face at last

utterson.title: Mr. Utterson
utterson.subtitle: Lawyer
fields: Countenance
Rugged, never lighted by a smile; cold, scanty and embarrassed in discourse; lean, long, dusty, dreary and yet somehow lovable.
Practice
Austere with himself — gin when alone, to mortify a taste for vintages. Frequently the last reputable acquaintance and the last good influence in the lives of downgoing men.
Creed
“I incline to Cain’s heresy: I let my brother go to the devil in his own way.”
The safe
Locks Hyde’s note away once Guest lays the two hands side by side — and keeps the secret with it.

enfield.title: Richard Enfield
enfield.subtitle: Man about town
fields: Standing
Utterson’s distant kinsman and Sunday-walk companion — a nut to crack for many, what the two see in each other.
His rule
“You start a question, and it’s like starting a stone… the more it looks like Queer Street, the less I ask.”

hyde.title: Edward Hyde
hyde.subtitle: Unknown · The man with the key
fields: The trampling
Ran calmly over a child’s body at a black winter crossing and left her screaming. “It wasn’t like a man; it was like some damned Juggernaut.”
The cheque
Settled the scandal at a hundred pounds — ten in gold and a cheque on Coutts’s, signed with a name very well known and often printed. The cheque was genuine.
Impression
Something displeasing, something downright detestable; a strong feeling of deformity, though no one can specify the point.
The Carew murder
Clubbed an aged, beautiful gentleman to the earth under the maid’s window, with ape-like fury — and was tracked to Soho, an hour gone.
The letter
“Your benefactor need labour under no alarm for my safety” — signed Edward Hyde, in a hand identical to the doctor’s, only sloped the other way.
Face to face

Pale and dwarfish; a displeasing smile; a murderous mixture of timidity and boldness; a husky, whispering and somewhat broken voice. “If ever I read Satan’s signature upon a face, it is on that of your new friend.”
His standing
Carries his own key to the door, and Dr. Jekyll’s servants have all orders to obey him. He mostly comes and goes by the laboratory.
rels: Dr. Jekyll · heir under the will
stage.locked: What he is to Dr. Jekyll

jekyll.title: Dr. Henry Jekyll
jekyll.subtitle: M.D., D.C.L. · The square
fields: At ease
A large, well-made, smooth-faced man of fifty, with every mark of capacity and kindness — host of pleasant dinners to old cronies, all judges of good wine.
The one condition
“The moment I choose, I can be rid of Mr. Hyde. I give you my hand upon that.” And he begs Utterson to let the matter sleep.
The letter
Swears he is done with Hyde in this world — but Poole knows of no messenger, and Utterson’s blood runs cold: “Henry Jekyll forge for a murderer!”
Seclusion
Two bright months of dinners and charity, then the door shuts even to Utterson. “I have brought on myself a punishment and a danger that I cannot name.”
jekyll.locked: Why his will names Edward Hyde

lanyon.title: Dr. Lanyon
lanyon.subtitle: Physician · Cavendish Square
fields: Manner
A hearty, healthy, dapper, red-faced gentleman with a shock of hair prematurely white and a boisterous and decided manner; a geniality somewhat theatrical, but resting on genuine feeling.
The estrangement
“It is more than ten years since Henry Jekyll became too fanciful for me… Such unscientific balderdash would have estranged Damon and Pythias.” Of Hyde he has never heard.
The shock
“I have had a shock, and I shall never recover.” Dead within a fortnight — leaving a sealed packet not to be opened till the death or disappearance of Henry Jekyll.
lanyon.locked: The right and wrong of this

poole.title: Poole
poole.subtitle: Butler · Jekyll’s household
fields: Post
A well-dressed, elderly servant at the door of the one house in the square still occupied entire.
Orders
“Mr. Hyde has a key… We have all orders to obey him.” Hyde never dines here; he comes and goes by the laboratory.

bystreet.title: The By-street
bystreet.subtitle: Street · A busy quarter
fields: Character

Small and what is called quiet, but driving a thriving trade on the weekdays; freshly painted shutters, well-polished brasses — it shone out in contrast to its dingy neighbourhood, like a fire in a forest.

door.title: The Door
door.subtitle: A sinister block of building
fields: The block
Two storeys high; no window, nothing but a door on the lower storey and a blind forehead of discoloured wall on the upper — the marks of prolonged and sordid negligence.
Neglect
Equipped with neither bell nor knocker, blistered and distained. Nobody goes in or out but, once in a great while, the gentleman of Enfield’s adventure.

gaunt.title: Gaunt Street
gaunt.subtitle: Utterson’s house
fields: Description
The lawyer’s bachelor house, close by a church whose bells ring conveniently near. Sunday evenings end here with a volume of dry divinity until the clock strikes twelve.

cavendish.title: Cavendish Square
cavendish.subtitle: The citadel of medicine
fields: Description
Where the great Dr. Lanyon has his house and receives his crowding patients.

soho.title: Soho
soho.subtitle: District
fields: The quarter
Muddy ways, slatternly passengers, a gin palace, a low French eating house — under the fog, like a district of some city in a nightmare.
Hyde’s rooms
Furnished with luxury and good taste — found ransacked in haste, pockets inside out, and a pile of grey ashes on the hearth.

square.title: The Square of Ancient Houses
square.subtitle: Square · Second from the corner
fields: Description

Ancient, handsome houses, now mostly decayed and let in flats and chambers — map-engravers, architects, shady lawyers. One house, second from the corner, is still occupied entire, with a great air of wealth and comfort.
The hall
Paved with flags, warmed like a country house by a bright open fire — Utterson calls it the pleasantest room in London.

carew.title: Sir Danvers Carew
carew.subtitle: M.P.
fields: The lane
An aged beautiful gentleman with white hair, accosting with a very pretty manner of politeness — struck down under the maid’s window.
Found on him
A purse, a gold watch, and a sealed and stamped envelope addressed to Mr. Utterson — no cards or papers besides.

guest.title: Mr. Guest
guest.subtitle: Head clerk
fields: Counsel
There is no man from whom Utterson keeps fewer secrets — a great student and critic of handwriting.
The comparison
Lays the murderer’s note beside the doctor’s dinner invitation: “the two hands are in many points identical: only differently sloped.”

lane.title: The Lane by the River
lane.subtitle: Scene of the crime
fields: That night
Brilliantly lit by the full moon and watched from the maid’s window — where the old gentleman bowed, and Mr. Hyde broke out of all bounds.

jekyll.excerpt: “If he be Mr. Hyde,” he had thought, “I shall be Mr. Seek.”
jekyll.body: The dry lawyer makes exactly one joke, and it turns him into a detective.

hyde.body: Everyone describes him by the feeling he leaves, never by a feature. Enfield, the doctor, the women — all wanted him dead on sight.

description: Mr. Utterson the lawyer follows a door, a will, and a name — Edward Hyde — into the private weather of his oldest friend. London, fog, and a question of character.
